statements.text: “West Virginians and all Americans deserve good service. When folks pick up the phone and ask for help, they shouldn’t have to deal with AI robots or be routed to someone across the world. This bill puts American workers first and ensures people can talk to a real person who understands them when they need help,”
statements.venue: Senate press release on Keep Call Centers in America Act

statements.text: “I’m not afraid of AI,” declared Senator Justice. “I am absolutely one to embrace the opportunities of the future.”

“One time we were scared to death when we were riding horses to get in an automobile. All of a sudden, we take off that way and then we were scared to death about getting in an airplane and everything,” said Senator Justice. “We couldn’t think about going to the moon and all the different things that we’ve done.”

“A.I. chatbots are an incredible tool for older Americans, but we can’t miss the opportunity to protect our seniors who rely on chatbots for support, companionship, and even important decisions during critical times. The Senior Chatbot Protection Act sets transparency standards, so our seniors know they are speaking with a chatbot and not a real person—whether in everyday conversations or when making high-stakes decisions.
statements.venue: Senate press release on Senior Chatbot Protection Act

statements.text: “The data centers, if they can’t exist within our state in a really great way from the standpoint of water or noise or electricity cost and all that kind of stuff, if they can’t pony up to the board and actually do their part, then they shouldn’t be here,”
statements.venue: WV Chamber of Commerce Business Summit, reported by WOAY

statements.text: “I oftentimes think about my dad. ‘Son, if you go into a restaurant and the waitress comes over and says sir, do you like your eggs scrambled or fried? What should you say? Yes,’" Justice said. "Think about it. Do we like our data center scrambled or fried? I would say yes. I would say there’s a way to have it all. There’s a way to have your cake and eat it too.”
statements.venue: Remarks at WV Chamber of Commerce annual meeting
